verdict.rationale: All x402/MPP evidence describes Crossmint wallets acting as the *payer* (agent) that pays a 402-protected endpoint owned by someone else — e.g. 'pay x402-protected endpoints using a Crossmint wallet' and the mppx client that 'pays via Tempo and retries the request.' There is no evidence of Crossmint providing seller-side tooling for a developer to put their own API behind a 402 paywall and receive per-call agent payments without a checkout UI.
